cs-en-buynet_en7

On the summary screen, check the details. The conversion details show the shekel amount being sold, and the currency the supplier receives. cs-en-buynet_en8

cs-en-buynet_en10

cs-en-exbuy4

cs-en-exbuy6

cs-en-fxfx2

cs-en-fxfx3

cs-en-fxfx4

cs-en-fxfx5

cs-en-fxfx7

In this guide we will run a transactions report from the system. The report shows all the transactions in your account, you can filter by dates and currency, and export to a PDF or Excel file.
cs-en-reports2
In the top menu, click Transactions, and choose Reports. If the page is showing in English, you can switch to Hebrew above the table.
cs-en-reports3
Above the table, choose the date range: from a date, and to a date. In the currency field, choose one currency, or leave all. Then click Generate.
cs-en-reports4

Each row in the report shows a reference number, a date, the transaction type, and the payment details. The credit column shows money that came into the account, and the debit column shows money that went out, or a fee. And on the left is the balance in each currency after the transaction.
cs-en-reports5
To save the report, click export to PDF, and you get a file for printing or sending. Or export to Excel, and you get a working file, for example for your bookkeeper.
cs-en-reports_orders

To see all your orders, in the Transactions menu choose Orders. Each row shows the order number, buy or sell, the amount, the rate, the date, the fee and the status. In the Confirmation column you can download the order confirmation. And for an order that is still waiting for its rate, you can switch to a real-time rate, or cancel it.
cs-en-reports7

To sum up: in Transactions, choose Reports, choose dates and currency, and click Generate. Then export the report to PDF or Excel. And if you have any questions, your Clearshift representative is happy to help.

In this guide we will set up a new supplier in the portal. Before the first payment to a supplier, you set them up once, and from then on they appear in your list of beneficiaries. On each screen you do the action, and only then move on.
cs-en-supplier2
In the top menu, click Settings, and choose Add Bank Account. If the form is showing in English, you can switch to Hebrew at the top of the form.
cs-en-supplier3
At the top of the form, choose third party, meaning a new supplier you pay. Under transaction type, choose business, if the supplier is a company, or private, if they are an individual.
cs-en-supplier4

Fill in the supplier’s details: the full official name, and the name in English. Choose the country where the business is registered. Then choose the type of ID number, and enter the number itself: the company’s registration number, or a tax ID. The name must be identical to the name on the supplier’s invoice.
cs-en-supplier5

Enter the supplier’s website, or their social media page. If there isn’t one, state that there isn’t. Add a short description of the supplier, for example, clothing manufacturer. And you can tick that the account holder will be notified when the money is sent to them.
cs-en-supplier6
In the business address field, start typing, and choose the address from the list. Then, in the bank account details, choose the bank’s country, and the account’s currency.
cs-en-supplier7

Now enter the supplier’s bank account details, from their invoice: the IBAN or account number, and the SWIFT code. Enter the bank name, and the bank account name, meaning the name the account is registered under. And choose a nickname for the account. This is the name that will appear in your list of beneficiaries. The fields change according to the country and currency you chose.
cs-en-supplier8

Choose the transfer purpose, meaning the reason for the payments to the supplier. Upload a document that shows the purpose of the payment, an invoice or a contract, and tick whether it shows the bank account details. Enter the estimated annual turnover, and the amount of the highest single payment. And under transfer direction, choose destination, because you are sending money to the supplier.
cs-en-supplier9

If the invoice doesn’t show the bank details, also upload here an official document with the supplier’s bank account details. Then click Create bank account. A new account is reviewed by our compliance team. You can already enter a payment, but it will wait until the account is approved.
cs-en-supplier_priv

If the supplier is a private individual, choose Private under transaction type. Fill in the first and last name, also in English, and choose the citizenship. Choose the type of I D document, enter its number, attach a copy, and enter the date of birth. The rest of the form is the same: address, bank account details, transfer purpose and documents.
cs-en-supplier_self

To add a bank account that is in your own name, choose Own at the top of the form. Here you fill in only the bank account details: country, currency, account name, bank name and account number. Upload a voided cheque or a bank statement, and choose the transfer direction: source, destination, or both directions.
cs-en-supplier12

To sum up: in Settings, choose Add Bank Account, third party, and business or private. Fill in the supplier’s details, their bank account details, and the transfer purpose, and upload a document. Click Create bank account, and after approval the supplier appears in your list of beneficiaries. And if you have any questions, your Clearshift representative is happy to help.

In this guide we will pay a supplier abroad in the same currency: we have dollars, and the supplier receives dollars. There is no conversion here, and no rate. On each screen you do the action, and only then move on.
cs-en-usdusd2
In the top menu, click New Order, and choose Payments. If the form is showing in English, you can switch to Hebrew at the top of the form.
cs-en-usdusd3

At the top of the form, choose the currencies. In the right-hand field, choose the currency the supplier receives, dollars. And in the field next to it, also choose dollars. This way there is no conversion, and the dollars go out as they are. Below there is a box for deducting the fee from the beneficiary. Tick it only if you agreed with the supplier that the fee comes off the amount they receive.
cs-en-usdusd4

In the payment details, in the bank account field, choose the account of your supplier abroad. In the amount field, enter how many dollars the supplier should receive, in the example five thousand dollars. In the transfer purpose field, choose the reason for the payment, for example, purchase of goods. And in the note to the beneficiary you can enter the invoice number.
cs-en-usdusd5

Under funding details, choose where the dollars come from. Choose balance, if the dollars are already in your Clearshift account. Or bank account, if you will transfer the dollars from your bank account. In the payment document field you can attach the supplier’s invoice. Then click Next.
cs-en-usdusd6

On the summary screen, check the details: the amount to pay, and the beneficiary’s name. Below is the fee for the transaction. And the recommended funding amount row shows how many dollars you need to transfer. The example shows zero, because the demo account already holds a dollar balance. There is no conversion here, so there is no rate: the supplier receives exactly the amount you entered.
cs-en-usdusd7
The breakdown shows the amount to pay, the fee, and your existing balance deducted. Tick the declaration, and click Place order.
cs-en-usdusd9

If you chose bank account, now transfer the amount in dollars to Clearshift, including the fee. If you paid from your balance, there is nothing to transfer. The supplier is paid once the account is fully funded, and you get an email update.
cs-en-usdusd11

To sum up: open an order in Payments, and choose dollars in both currency fields. Choose the beneficiary, enter the amount, and confirm. Verify by WhatsApp or SMS. Fund with dollars, or pay from your balance, and the payment goes out to the supplier. And if you have any questions, your Clearshift representative is happy to help.
